sso.owner.guide: How to set it up (step by step)
sso.guide.google.1: Open console.cloud.google.com and pick a project (or create a new one).
sso.guide.google.2: In the menu: Google Auth Platform. The first time, click Get started and fill in an app name and support email.
sso.guide.google.3: Branding: name, logo, support email, home page, links to the privacy policy and terms, and Authorized domains with your domain.
sso.guide.google.4: Audience: user type External. At the end click Publish app, otherwise only test users can sign in.
sso.guide.google.5: Data access: only openid, email and profile. These are basic scopes, so no Google review is needed.
sso.guide.google.6: Clients: click Create client, type Web application, and paste the redirect URI above in Authorized redirect URIs.
sso.guide.google.7: Copy the Client ID and Client secret (the secret is shown only when created), paste them here, save and click "Test connection".
sso.guide.microsoft.1: Open entra.microsoft.com (or portal.azure.com), then Entra ID → App registrations → New registration.
sso.guide.microsoft.2: Supported account types: choose Any Entra ID Tenant + Personal Microsoft accounts.
sso.guide.microsoft.3: Redirect URI: type Web, paste the redirect URI above. Click Register.
sso.guide.microsoft.4: On the Overview page copy the Application (client) ID.
sso.guide.microsoft.5: Certificates & secrets: click New client secret and copy its Value (not the Secret ID). It lasts up to 24 months, so note when to renew it.
sso.guide.microsoft.6: Token configuration: Add optional claim, type ID, select email and xms_edov. Without them work accounts cannot sign in, because the email cannot be trusted.
sso.guide.microsoft.7: Recommended: Branding & properties → Publisher verification. Without it some organizations ask for an admin's approval.
sso.guide.microsoft.8: Paste the client ID and the secret here. Leave Tenant empty (common). Save and click "Test connection".
